items.text: EX-99.1 2 amzn-20260930xex991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 AMAZON.COM ANNOUNCES THIRD QUARTER RESULTS Operating income was $28.1 billion and operating margin was 13.9%-Amazon's highest operating margin ever AWS net sales increased 39.3%-its fastest growth in nearly five years-to a $184 billion annualized revenue run rate SEATTLE-(BUSINESS WIRE) October 29, 2026-Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ AMZN) today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Net sales increased 12% to $201.9 billion in the third quarter, compared with $180.2 billion in third quarter 2025. Excluding the $0.9 billion unfavorable impact from year-over-year changes in foreign exchange rates throughout the quarter, net sales increased 13% compared with third quarter 2025. As a reminder, Prime Day timing shifted this year, with the event occurring in Q2 for most large countries. In 2025, Prime Day occurred entirely in Q3. Excluding this shift, third quarter year-over-year growth would have been approximately 400 basis points higher. North America segment sales increased 6% year-over-year to $112.9 billion. International segment sales increased 5% year-over-year to $43.1 billion, or increased 8% excluding changes in foreign exchange rates. AWS segment sales increased 39% year-over-year to $46.0 billion. Operating income increased to $28.1 billion in the third quarter, compared with $17.4 billion in third quarter 2025. North America segment operating income was $8.7 billion, compared with $4.8 billion in third quarter 2025. International segment operating income was $1.6 billion, compared with $1.2 billion in third quarter 2025. AWS segment operating income was $17.8 billion, compared with $11.4 billion in third quarter 2025. Net income decreased to $20.7 billion in the third quarter, or $1.89 per diluted share, compared with $21.2 billion, or $1.95 per diluted share, in third quarter 2025. This decrease is driven primarily by pre-tax gains of $9.5 billion in third quarter 2025 included in non-operating income (expense) from our investments in Anthropic. Operating cash flow increased 29% to $168.3 billion for the trailing twelve months, compared with $130.7 billion for the trailing twelve months ended September 30, 2025. Free cash flow decreased to an outflow of $42.4 billion for the trailing twelve months, driven primarily by a year-over-year increase of $94.8 billion in purchases of property and equipment, net of proceeds from sales and incentives. This increase primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence. This compares to free cash flow inflow of $14.8 billion for the trailing twelve months ended September 30, 2025. "Our AWS investment in functionality and infrastructure is working, with over 39% year-over-year revenue growth in Q3 ($184 billion revenue run rate) and projected revenue growth rates of over 40% both in 2027 and in 2028," said Andy Jassy, President and CEO, Amazon. "Our broader selection and speedier delivery are helping us capture more retail market segment share with improving margins, and our newer businesses, ranging from Grocery to Pharmacy to Amazon Leo to Zoox are progressing encouragingly. There has never been a trillion dollar revenue business, and we may have two of them in the next 5-10 years." items.text: EX-99.1 2 ex-9913q26rivianearningspr.htm EX-99.1 Document Rivian Releases Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Generated $2.155 billion in revenue, a 38 percent increase year-over-year Deliveries up 46 percent year-over-year with R2 already the best-selling Rivian vehicle by volume, outselling both R1 and EDV in the third quarter Given Rivian's strong performance, the company is improving 2026 guidance across all metrics Irvine, California, October 29, 2026 Rivian Automotive, Inc. (NASDAQ RIVN), an American automotive technology company that develops and manufactures category-defining electric vehicles as well as vertically integrated technologies and offers a suite of value-added services, today announced its third quarter 2026 financial results. RJ Scaringe, Rivian Founder and CEO, said "We had great results with R2 becoming our best selling vehicle by volume in the third quarter. Customer and media feedback on R2 has been exceptional. Regarding our technology roadmap, our autonomy platform is progressing rapidly, and we are super excited about Point to Point. We are laying the foundations for a future that we believe will be fully electric, autonomous and AI defined. I could not be more excited about the opportunity ahead for Rivian." Business Highlights Rivian achieved record production volumes in Normal, Illinois as it continued to ramp R2 manufacturing. The company had record deliveries of 19,248 units with R2 delivering much of the gain quarter-over-quarter. R2 is already the best-selling Rivian vehicle, outselling both R1 and EDV in the third quarter. R2 continues to generate rave reviews and awards from the media and recently won Top Gear's SUV of the Year for 2027. Rivian continues to innovate with software and AI. With the Rivian Assistant, Rivian has developed a smarter and more customizable AI-defined vehicle experience for R1 and R2 owners. Net sales increased 1.0% to $1,602 million in the third quarter, exceeding the Company's outlook of a 1% decline and reflecting the benefits of the 2025 strategic portfolio actions. Organic sales grew 5.1%, well above the Company's 3% outlook, with growth across all three divisions, driven primarily by volume growth of 4.6%, as well as positive price and mix of 0.5%. Rick Dierker, Chief Executive Officer, commented, “Our power brands continue to perform exceptionally well despite a challenging macroeconomic environment, driving our third consecutive quarter of industry-leading organic sales growth. In the third quarter, our leading brands once again increased share driven by innovation, distribution wins, and our targeted marketing investments. The strength of our brand portfolio, combined with our targeted 2025 strategic portfolio actions, has enhanced the focus on our growth initiatives and reinforces our confidence as we enter the fourth quarter of 2026 and into 2027. We are raising our 2026 outlook for sales and tightening our outlook for earnings per share. “Thank you to our Church & Dwight team members across the globe for executing well in a volatile environment and delivering strong organic growth and gross margin expansion every quarter this year. In the third quarter, the domestic division grew 4.4% organically reflecting sustained strength across both our household and personal care portfolios.
